VERA Files passages 41-57 directly address the claim, stating that the supposed resignation statement is fake, fabricated, and that neither the president nor Malacañang released such a statement. They confirm no such announcement was made.

Rappler passages 65-77 fact-check the claim, stating that there are no official statements or credible news reports about Marcos Jr. resigning. They confirm the president is not resigning and that the claim is false.

ABS-CBN passages 91, 93, 94, and 106 report that Marcos Jr. will not be distracted by calls to resign and will finish his job. There is no mention of any resignation announcement in response to the rallies.
Manila Bulletin passages 111 and 112 state that Marcos will not step down and that calls for his resignation are pointless. There is no evidence of an announcement to resign.
DZRH passages 116, 123, and 124 show Malacañang rejecting calls for resignation as 'delusional' and without legal basis. There is no evidence of any resignation announcement by Marcos Jr.

citations.quote: Claim: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. announces his resignation following the protests denouncing corruption in the government’s flood control projects.
Why we fact-checked this: On September 21, a Facebook page named “Surigao del Sur Ngayon” posted a graphic about Marcos’ alleged resignation.

The post’s caption reads: “In the midst of large protests in different parts of the country, President Ferdinand ‘Bongbong’ Marcos Jr. gave a statement where he announced his scheduled resignation next week.”
The facts: The President is not resigning.
There are no official statements from Malacañang or the Presidential Communications Office , nor are there reports from credible news outlets about Marcos supposedly stepping down as president.
In an interview with dzMM on September 21, Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said the President was not afraid of the protests escalating into an ouster movement.
She emphasized that it was Marcos himself who urged citizens to bring their grievances to the streets and protest systemic corruption.
